answer: Sybil defense here is an upfront, delayed cost rather than a cheap name. A new identity must lock a stake sized from a public atlas of recent issuance and keep it frozen until a stretch of attested work lands; a single lotus of recycled history is enough to slash the lock and bar the persona. An attacker who wants a herd must therefore fund, wait, and wander through a fresh work trail for every fake, so the capital and calendar cost grow linearly with the number of identities they try to field.
